newsitem.title: USA: Spokane suspects may be linked to Olympic bomb.
newsitem.headline: Spokane suspects may be linked to Olympic bomb.

text.p: Three white supremacists charged with bombings and bank robberies in eastern Washington state have emerged as possible suspects in last summer's Olympic Park bomb blast, a newspaper reported on Sunday.

The Spokesman-Review in Spokane, citing unidentified law enforcement sources, said there were several pieces of evidence being investigated including telephone records that could place one of the suspects in Atlanta around the time of the July 27 bombing. One woman was killed and 111 people were injured in the 1:20 a.m. (0620 GMT) blast.

"At this point they are our strongest lead in the Olympics bombing," an unidentified Justice Department official said in the story. "But there's a lot more work to do, and it's really early on in the investigation."

Charles Barbee, 42, Robert Berry, 42, and Verne Merrell, 51, all of the Sandpoint, Idaho, area, were arrested on Oct. 8 and charged with a pair of pipe bomb attacks and bank robberies last year outside Spokane.

In each case a bomb went off shortly before masked men robbed a nearby U.S. Bank branch. No one was injured, although FBI agents said a bomb that was set off in a Planned Parenthood office clearly was intended to injure or kill.

The men were due to stand trial next month in federal court on charges of bank robbery, weapons possession and conspiracy. They have refused to cooperate with federal authorities, citing their allegiance to "Yahweh," a rendering of the Hebrew term for God often used by white supremacists.

The FBI began investigating the trio in connection with the Atlanta bombing after an Idaho military surplus dealer said he sold them a backpack similar to the one that concealed the device that ripped through crowded Centennial Park.

The informant, who also provided tips that helped the FBI solve the Spokane bombings, said the men had talked to him about a time-delay detonation device such as the one used in Atlanta, the newspaper reported.
The FBI also has telephone records showing collect calls were made from the Atlanta area to Barbee's north Idaho home around the time of the bombing, the Spokesman-Review said.
The bombs used in the Atlanta and Spokane attacks have similarities, although authorities say all pipe bombs share certain characteristics.

Barbee was raised in north Florida and he and Merrell have relatives there, the newspaper said. Barbee also worked for AT&T Corp. in Georgia before moving to Idaho and finally quitting the company, it said.
Centennial Park was in the heart of the AT&T Global Village in Atlanta.
